provenance.author: Riven
provenance.method: Original art painted by tools/content/painters.py from these definitions; behaviour reimplemented from observed modern Minecraft gameplay. No Mojang code, textures, models or sounds.
provenance.riven-resources: Textures under riven-resources/ are original commissioned Riven artwork from the Riven Resources project, imported unchanged under Riven's terms (NRR-1.0); each set's PROVENANCE.md names its source archive and hash.

contract: Riven's own content (blocks, items and their assets). Every block declares an id (registry riven:<id>), a kind that selects its Java implementation, its English name, creative tab, hardness, resistance, harvest tool and level, behaviour values for its kind, and textures by name.

textures: each named texture comes from a painter in tools/content/painters.py (with fixed args, or expanded over 'for' values) or a committed file under tools/content/; a name with {placeholders} expands over its 'for' values. tools/content/build_content.py writes blockstates, models, item models, textures and the lang file under assets/riven from this file, and --check proves the committed assets match.

kinds. stone: a full rock block, either one texture by name (all) or Riven Resources face sets (textures.source, a folder under tools/content/, and faces: all, or side and top with the top also below; the main set first), one set by position so wide walls do not repeat. pointed_dripstone: a stalactite (direction down) or stalagmite (direction up) whose thickness (tip_merge, tip, frustum, middle, base) follows its neighbours along its direction. A stalactite that loses the block it hangs from falls; a falling piece hurts what it lands on with fallDamagePerBlock per block fallen, at most fallDamageMax, and breaks on landing. A stalagmite that loses its base breaks. Landing on a stalagmite tip deals fall damage for the distance plus stalagmiteExtraFallBlocks, times stalagmiteDamageMultiplier. A stalactite tip drips water or lava (dripChance per display tick) when that fluid sits on top of the block its column hangs from, and a water drip fills a cauldron up to cauldronReachBlocks below (cauldronFillChance per random tick). The same kind serves every pointed formation material (pointed_ice, pointed_salt, pointed_basalt): a piece's thickness follows only neighbours of its own block, so two materials never merge into one column.

ores: one block riven:ore_<mineral> per mineral, its host property indexing hosts (Riven's host stones); each state draws its host stone's face sets, one by position as the host shows them, under an overlay (ore_overlay_<shine>) tinted with the mineral's color. With GTCEu, a mineral naming a gregtech material drops that material's GTCEu ore, so GTCEu processing applies; otherwise the block drops itself. Minerals with gregtech null are Supersymmetry minerals GTCEu lacks.

unstable: one block riven:unstable_<host> per host rock, named Unstable <host>: the host's own faces under an untinted crack overlay (overlay, a texture). block and meta name the host's registered state (what it drops and how it maps), terrain the generator's rock (TerrainBlock) it replaces where a cave floor is unstable (riven-cave-decor.json unstable), and dust the colour of the dust it sheds into open space below (dustChance per display tick). A Riven host takes its block's face sets and name; another names its textures (all, or top, bottom and side). A player who steps or lands on it without sneaking sets it off: it creaks and, after triggerDelayTicks, the unstable stone joined to it within spreadRadiusBlocks (at most maximumBlocks, any host) falls ring by ring outward, spreadTicksPerBlock apart, each column from the bottom up. A falling piece hurts what it lands on (fallDamagePerBlock per block fallen, at most fallDamageMax) and shatters, dropping its host's drops at debrisDropChance. Mined it drops its host's drops; silk touch keeps it, and placed again it behaves the same. Unstable stone holds otherwise: no neighbour change or missing support sets it off.

woods.about: Tree sets from Riven Resources (Decoration Library 01, and Art Requisition 02 for the species naming it as their source and for every species' planks; see each folder's PROVENANCE.md), textures unchanged. Each species registers log_<id> (bark sides, end-grain caps, any axis), leaves_<id> (its two foliage textures at random, cutout, decaying away from logs, dropping its sapling 1 in saplingChance), sapling_<id> (grows into one of the wood's riven-trees.json species, four in a square into its 2 x 2 species where it has one), litter_<id> (a thin ground decal with no collision that plants and blocks replace) and planks_<id>; a log crafts into four of its planks and smelts to charcoal. architecture names the wood's form (broadleaf, conifer, palm or fern; a palm's sapling also takes sand); riven-trees.json draws its trees.

decorations.about: Ground decorations from Riven Resources (Decoration Library 01, Art Requisitions 02 and 03; see each folder's PROVENANCE.md), textures unchanged. Each subject registers one block: plant_<id> (crossed planes, offset within its block like vanilla flowers), decal_<id> (a thin plane on the ground like leaf litter), tall_<id> (a two-block plant whose bottom and top pieces join, its form chosen where it grows) or cane_<id> (stem pieces stacked under a top piece like sugar cane, standing only where water lies beside its ground; each piece drops a sugar cane). A plant or decal shows one of its four forms by position. ground names what it stands on (grass, dirt including mud, sand, gravel, snow, stone, sandstone of either colour); without that ground it drops. replaceable ones give way to placed blocks, like tall grass. None has collision; all burn like vanilla plants but those marked flammable false. riven-ground-cover.json places them.

rocks.about: Rocks of the deep realms and their boundaries from Art Requisition 05 (riven-resources/requisition-05, PROVENANCE.md), textures unchanged. Each registers one block that shows its main or alternate face by position, so wide walls of one rock do not repeat; light is the level it gives (moonstone, molten seams, soul ash, the heat-cracked boundary), animated faces keep their frames. riven-realms.json places them.
